newsitem.title: UK: British interest rates left unchanged.
newsitem.headline: British interest rates left unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of England signalled that it had left official interest rates unchanged at 6.0 percent on Thursday by conducting routine money market operations at unchanged dealing rates.

It provided liquidity to the banking system at the established rate of 5-15/16 percent, indicating that finance minister Kenneth Clarke had ordered that rates should be left unchanged at his monthly monetary meeting with Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Wednesday.
The two men have been at odds over monetary policy since December.

George, who fears a resurgence in inflation in the next 18 months, argued unsuccessfully for an immediate quarter-point rate rise in December and warned that he would otherwise probably advise a half-point increase in January or February.

Clarke, the Chancellor of the Exchequer, is anxious to avoid raising rates in the run-up to the looming election as this would mean dearer home loans for millions of Britons. He argues that the economic signals are mixed.

Economists said official figures released on Thursday, showing manufacturing output grew just 0.2 percent in December, would help to justify Clarke's argument that there is little immediate risk of the economy overheating.
